title: App Startup, Lazy Initialisation, and DI Cost Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies app startup, lazy initialisation, and di cost?
options: Keep only measured essential initialization on startup and give lazy components explicit ownership and failure semantics.
Assume Lazy guarantees no eager request
questions.answer: Keep only measured essential initialization on startup and give lazy components explicit ownership and failure semantics.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: App Startup automatically moves every initializer off the main thread.
questions.explanation: Wrapping an expensive SDK in App Startup centralises it but still executes the cost on the application startup path.

questions.prompt: What question determines whether an initializer belongs at app startup?
questions.answer: Must this work complete before the first meaningful UI/action, or can its owning feature initialise it later?
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
